meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.

examples.trans: Nobody here will touch you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.
Tell me what happened.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Russian').

examples.text: Я русский язык вообще не знаю.
examples.trans: I do not know the Russian language at all.
Samson, are you Russian?
I speak Russian.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'language; tongue' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я русский язык вообще не знаю.
examples.trans: I do not know the Russian language at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: Actually, he died recently.

examples.text: Я русский язык вообще не знаю.

examples.text: Как ты вообще мог это сделать?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('what').

examples.trans: She knew nothing about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to carry, to take', paired with 'нести'.

examples.trans: Which room did they carry him to?

examples.trans: Do not be afraid, you will manage on your own.

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'run', paired with 'побежать'.

examples.trans: Did another husband run away from you?

meanings.en: to save, to rescue from danger
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'save / rescue', paired with 'спасти'.

examples.trans: Run to the room, save Denis!

examples.text: Все прибежали тебя спасать — и я, и папа!
examples.trans: Everyone came running to save you — both me and Dad!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will save', paired with 'спасать'.

examples.text: Твоя кухня могла бы спасти положение.
examples.trans: Your cuisine could save the situation.

examples.text: Все деньги пойдут на спасение животных.
examples.trans: All the money will go toward saving the animals.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'рода'). Common feminine noun meaning 'nature' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ладно, только ради тебя и природы.

examples.text: Кто, как не мы, поддержит природу?
